carpet.floooring: Gustav "Brick" Floooring arrived on Day 4 and found the section asleep. The welcome had to wait until somebody needed the kettle.
Gustav "Brick" Floooring shaved using a spoon for a mirror. One side looks ready for inspection. The other looks ready for winter.

A bullet clipped Gustav "Brick" Floooring's helmet at R-F2 and took a strip of scalp with it. He bled into his collar, swore, and lay low. Shot by Rafael Davidsonmars of the Concord (@davidsonmarshall). The Hegemony flag went up over Hill 304. Gustav "Brick" Floooring did not cheer. He sat down on a sandbag and ate his ration slowly, like a man with time again.
Gustav "Brick" Floooring sat out the day with a bandaged arm, cleaning every rifle within reach. It was the only job the medic would allow.
The medics cleaned Gustav "Brick" Floooring's wound one last time and pronounced him fit. He is back to full duty at R-F2.
Gustav "Brick" Floooring fired short bursts at the gap in the enemy wire, the way the sergeant taught. Valentin Jarg was badly wounded trying to cross it.

Dawn watch. Gustav "Brick" Floooring put a round across no man's land and the enemy line went quiet: Hugo Luissantos, grazed. Gustav "Brick" Floooring was hit in the hand while passing a mug along the trench at R-F2. He did not spill a drop. The men are still talking about that. Shot by Rafael Davidsonmars of the Concord (@davidsonmarshall).
christianbarefoot3440: Bastian Christianbar, a farmhand from Northwick, was sent forward on Day 5 to fill a gap in S-F1. The gap had a name once. Nobody says it.

A splinter opened Bastian Christianbar's cheek at S-F1. A medic stitched it on the spot and he was back on the fire step before the tea went cold. A letter from home found Bastian Christianbar before the night shift. Bastian Christianbar folded it small and kept it close. Hill 304 is in Hegemony hands. Bastian Christianbar stopped arguing about the next watch and went to check the stores.
The medics cleaned Bastian Christianbar's wound one last time and pronounced him fit. He is back to full duty at S-F1.
At Blackwater Canal, Bastian Christianbar of the Concord and Emil Potato of the Hegemony spent the morning shooting at the same loose sheet of metal. The sheet kept winning.
Bastian Christianbar gave Karel Adauto the last match in the trench. Karel used it to light a candle so that Bastian could finish a letter.
Bastian Christianbar's spoon vanished during supper. He scratched a mark into a replacement and began keeping a closer eye on the washing bucket.
dravci85: Bram "Ghost" Dravci took the place of a man nobody would talk about. The dugout still had his blanket. He kept it folded.
The First Wave ribbon marked Bram "Ghost" Dravci as an early volunteer. At S-F14, a newcomer asked what those first days had been like.
Day 3: Verdel Ridge was lost. Bram "Ghost" Dravci wrote down the news without trying to explain it.
Bram "Ghost" Dravci watched a pale shape beyond the wire while a flare burned out. It turned out to be a sack, right where the sack had always been.
Bram "Ghost" Dravci sorted the dressings by lamplight. When the next stretcher arrived, he could find everything without looking.

Bram "Ghost" Dravci opened a parcel addressed in unfamiliar handwriting. A note inside said the usual writer had hurt a wrist. He read that note first. Hill 304 has been won. Bram "Ghost" Dravci listened as the corporal read the news twice, once for the men just off watch.
Bram "Ghost" Dravci ended a letter with 'nothing to report', then added half a page about the missing soap.
A bullet found Bram "Ghost" Dravci at S-F14, high in the shoulder. He went down hard and stayed down. Shot by Clement Tsanev of the Concord (@vl.tsanev).
A medic stopped by Bram "Ghost" Dravci's stretcher every few hours for a week. Today the medic found it empty. Bram "Ghost" Dravci had gone back to S-F14.

Bram "Ghost" Dravci was hit in the hand while passing a mug along the trench at S-F14. He did not spill a drop. The men are still talking about that. Shot by Tobias "Crow" Cowboii of the Concord (@the_cowboii).
